rationale: The available literature directly establishing spinocerebellar ataxia 52 (SCA52; OMIM #621535) demonstrates that the core, defining phenotypic presentation of heterozygous RAB3A pathogenic variants (specifically the c.247C>T, p.Arg83Trp mutation identified in two families) is adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar ataxia with cerebellar atrophy (accentuated in the vermis), accompanied in some individuals by mild gait spasticity and tremor. Neurodevelopmental manifestations were explicitly reported as 'variable features of neurodevelopmental disorders' rather than obligatory or fully penetrant findings. Consequently, developmental delay, cognitive impairment, or hypotonia cannot serve as mandatory inclusion criteria to identify or diagnose SCA52.

evidence.text: In two families carrying the heterozygous RAB3A c.247C>T (p.Arg83Trp) variant, affected individuals presented with adult-onset, slowly progressive cerebellar ataxia, cerebellar atrophy, and variable features of neurodevelopmental disorders, indicating that neurodevelopmental signs are non-obligate and exhibit phenotypic heterogeneity.

source.quote: Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors. Variable features of neurodevelopmental disorders were also observed.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance and spectrum of specific neurodevelopmental phenotypes (e.g., formal IQ assessment, language delay, childhood motor milestones) across all known heterozygous RAB3A variant carriers across diverse pedigrees?
new_directions.rationale: Currently, only a limited number of families (such as the two described by Miyamoto et al.) harboring the p.Arg83Trp variant have been published; systematic multi-center deep phenotyping is required to quantify the exact numerator and denominator of cognitive and neurodevelopmental features.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-R83W variants in RAB3A that disrupt GTP binding or effector interaction cause a distinct congenital/early-onset neurodevelopmental syndrome rather than adult-onset SCA52?
new_directions.rationale: R83W selectively impairs RIM1 and Rabphilin-3A binding while retaining GTP-binding affinity. Other pathogenic alterations in different functional domains might produce more severe, obligate neurodevelopmental deficits.
